publicTrace: Base rate / reference class: The post-expanded-CTC SPM child poverty series (2022–2024) has averaged 13.2 pct, with the 2024 print at 13.4 pct and a recent year-over-year change of −0.3 pct. The 2022–2024 range spans roughly 12.4–13.7 pct, establishing the empirical reference class for a 'no-major-policy-shock' year.

Point estimate mechanism: A weighted blend of the PolicyEngine current-law prior (13.0 pct, weight 0.55), post-expansion Census history (13.2 pct, weight 0.35), and the latest published print (13.4 pct, weight 0.10) yields a raw blend of ~13.1 pct; a macro adjustment of −0.05 pct for modest real-income growth and continued SNAP/Medicaid participation produces a calibrated point estimate of 13.0 pct.

Uncertainty widening: The PolicyEngine input is a stored prior, not a fresh microsimulation; Census SPM tables were not machine-readable at fetch time. Both data paths are incomplete, so uncertainty is explicitly widened beyond the prototype calibration half-widths (lower 1.1 pct, upper 1.3 pct) to reflect model and sampling risk.

Disconfirming consideration (upside risk): A significant rollback of SNAP, Medicaid, or housing assistance in 2025 budget legislation, or a labor-market softening that reduces earned-income tax credit receipts, could push the rate above 14.3 pct and outside the 80% interval.

Disconfirming consideration (downside risk): An unexpectedly strong labor market, expanded refundable credits, or higher-than-expected EITC/CTC take-up could push the rate below 11.9 pct, also outside the interval.

CDF shape note: The distribution is left-skewed relative to the point estimate because the post-expansion floor around 12–13 pct is well-established, while upside tail risk from policy retrenchment is fatter than downside risk from further improvement.

Calibration transparency: The median derived from the CDF (~12.1 pct) is slightly below the point estimate (13.0 pct) due to the asymmetric tail; the 80% interval spans approximately 11.2–15.1 pct, consistent with widened uncertainty from incomplete data paths.
assumptions: PolicyEngine current-law prior of 13.0 pct is treated as a valid seed but not a fresh microsimulation; it receives 0.55 weight in the blend.
No major mid-year legislative changes to SNAP, Medicaid, EITC, or CTC are assumed to have taken full-year effect in calendar 2025 under current law.
ASEC sampling error for the SPM child poverty rate is approximately ±0.5 pct at 90% confidence, contributing to the widened interval.
SPM expense and resource components (MOOP, housing, work expenses) are assumed to evolve in line with recent CPI and wage trends, without structural breaks.
The Census September 2026 release will cover calendar year 2025 income and poverty, consistent with the stated release schedule.
dataCaveats: Census SPM data tables were fetched live but the child-poverty history is a prototype seed; no machine-readable SPM table endpoint was confirmed, so historical series accuracy is not guaranteed.

PolicyEngine input confirms current-law status (API v0.654.1) but does not represent a fresh server-side microsimulation for this specific cell; the 13.0 pct prior may not reflect 2025-specific policy parameters.
SPM estimates incorporate geographic housing cost adjustments and medical out-of-pocket expenses, making them sensitive to regional price changes not captured in the macro adjustment.
Any 2025 legislative changes to refundable tax credits or means-tested transfers enacted after the PolicyEngine snapshot would not be reflected in the prior.
drivers: SNAP and Medicaid enrollment levels and benefit generosity in 2025
EITC and CTC refundability and take-up rates under current law
Labor market conditions affecting earned income among families with children
Medical out-of-pocket expense trends affecting SPM resource thresholds
Geographic housing cost adjustments in the SPM threshold methodology
